# Notation and conventions

## Genotype orientation {#sec-coding}

The standard numeric input uses `-1` and `1` for the two homozygotes and `0`
for the heterozygote. The allele represented by `1` depends on the input and its
orientation metadata. Do not infer a biological reference allele from the sign
alone. The first chapter uses an already coded maize dataset and shows the
entry point for importing your own files. The
[genotype input chapter](input.qmd) examines format-specific conversion and
orientation checks in detail.

Markers occupy rows in the numeric input table, whereas outputs such as
`genetic_values()` use individuals in rows. Align identifiers whenever combining
outputs instead of assuming that two objects share their row order.

## Symbols used in the first chapter

| Symbol | Meaning | Scale |
|---|---|---|
| $x_{ij}$ | Coded genotype | `-1`, `0`, `1` |
| $b_j$ | Raw additive effect series | Before component normalization |
| $c_i$ | Unscaled marker score | Sum of marker contributions |
| $\pi$ | Requested layer variance allocation | Package simulation scale |
| $g_i$ | Realized genetic value | After component normalization |
| $e_i$ | Realized residual | After residual normalization |
| $y_i$ | Realized phenotype | Genetic value plus residual in this example |
| $s_g^2$, $s_e^2$, $s_y^2$ | Sample variances | Denominator $n-1$ |
| $s_{ge}$ | Sample covariance | Denominator $n-1$ |
| $R_G$ | Realized genetic-to-phenotypic variance ratio | Diagnostic, not an estimated parameter |

The derivation in @sec-variance-derivation defines these sample quantities
explicitly. Later methods chapters will distinguish additive breeding values,
total genetic values, estimated breeding values, and genotypic effects in their
own model contexts.

## Two kinds of replication

`n_reps` requests simulation replications, represented by `rep` in phenotype
tables. The separate `reps` argument concerns entry-mean records and residual
scaling. They answer different experimental questions. The
[trait values chapter](trait.qmd) demonstrates both rather than treating them
as interchangeable ways to increase the number of observations.

## A function is not a method

`select_ind()` exposes several selection methods; `predict_ebv()` has different
relationship and trait configurations. Conversely, a single scientific method
can involve many internal functions. The [coverage register](functions.qmd)
therefore tracks public functions and method options separately.
